title: Should a source without sizes use the img's sizes (like WebKit)?

labels.name: interop
labels.description: Implementations are not interoperable with each other

body: ### What is the issue with the HTML Standard? https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/images.html#parse-a-sizes-attribute parses a `source`'s `sizes`: > Let _unparsed sizes list_ be the result of parsing a comma-separated list of component values from the value of _element_'s sizes attribute (or the empty string, if the attribute is absent). So a `source` without `sizes` gets 100vw, and https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/embedded-content.html#the-source-element requires `sizes` unless the `img` allows auto-sizes: > If, additionally, the following sibling `img` element does not allow auto-sizes, the `sizes` attribute must be present. (With #13211, an omitted `sizes` is `auto` when the `img` allows auto-sizes.) WebKit instead [uses the `img`'s `sizes`](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/15cb3560da6c863025957fce3ee065cf61902e75/Source/WebCore/html/HTMLImageElement.cpp#L324-L325) for a `source` without `sizes`, since https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/commit/8ef7d8dc0caad77eb47a4189b0a123939429073b. For ``, Safari TP 255 picks small.png, while Chrome Canary and Firefox Nightly pick large.png. With `` that isn't rendered yet, Safari TP uses 300px where the others use 100vw (the "Unrendered img…" subtest in web-platform-tests/wpt#64904). WebKit's approach allows DRYer markup when `source`s differ only in `type` or `media` and would repeat the same `sizes`, which seems nice. (Follow-up from [#13211 Q1](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13211#issuecomment-6953738920).)
